info.bio:
Big Country es una banda de rock de Dunfermline, Scotland, muy popular a comienzos de los ochenta hasta mediados de esa decada aun siguen editando material para sus seguidores.

La banda de rock, Big Country, la formó el presentador Stuart Adamson en 1981 en Escocia. Con los guitarristas Bruce Watson, Clive Parker, el bajista Tony Butler y el batería Mark Brzezicki, el grupo lanzó el single “Harvest Home”, seguido por “Fields of Fire”, que llegó al Top Ten en Inglaterra.

scenes.name: Nueva psicodelia y big music: Echo & the Bunnymen y U2
scenes.book: Postpunk. Romper todo y empezar de nuevo
scenes.author: Simon Reynolds
scenes.desc: En lugar de descender a lo oscuro, elevarse hacia la luz. Liverpool, que no tuvo punk clásico ni postpunk experimental, quería que la música fuera «una fiesta» (Bill Drummond, Zoo): el club Eric's, las bandas fantasma (The Crucial Three, Big in Japan), Wah! Heat, The Teardrop Explodes de Julian Cope. Echo & the Bunnymen, con el minimalismo aprendido de Television y la voz de Ian McCulloch, graban Crocodiles y Heaven Up Here, respuesta luminosa a Closer, y heredan el público huérfano de Joy Division; Ocean Rain los vuelve estrellas pop. U2, «punk positivo» cristiano y pacifista, guitarra de The Edge como sintetizador, quiere ocupar el lugar de Curtis: War (1983), «Sunday Bloody Sunday» en MTV, The Unforgettable Fire con Eno. Alrededor, la «big music» celta de Simple Minds, The Waterboys, Big Country y la neopsicodelia de The Blue Orchids.

podcast.title: Commercial Success
podcast.body: The band experienced its most successful years in the 1980s, maintaining a dedicated cult following until their breakup in 2000. They briefly reunited in 2007 and again in 2010. "Big countries best years were in the 80s, although they maintained a cult following through to their breakup in 2000. There was a brief reunion in 2007 and then another one in 2010."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Distinctive Sound
podcast.body: Big Country's sound was immediately recognizable for its guitars, which were made to sound like bagpipes, and its martial rhythm tracks. "Big Country was immediately recognizable by the guitar that sounded like bagpipes and their martial rhythm tracks."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Dread Zeppelin Fan
podcast.body: Stewart Adamson, a member of the band Big Country, was noted as a big fan of Dread Zeppelin. "Steward Adamson, a big country, remember them? He was a big fan of these guys."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Stuart Adamson's Tragic Death
podcast.body: Co-founder Stuart Adamson was not involved in any of the band's reunions; he tragically took his own life in 2001 after years of struggling with alcohol abuse and depression. "Stuart Adamson sadly is not part of any of these reunions because he took his own life in 2001 after years of alcohol abuse and depression."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Influence on Kid Rock's Vision
xref.body: Hank Williams was cited by Kid Rock as an influence on his musical vision, which he described as "very white trash Public Enemy style rap, plus The Stooges, plus Kiss, plus Hank Williams," also noting Kid Rock's admiration for country music. "A vision he calls very white trash public enemy style rap, plus the stooge's plus kiss plus Hank Williams. Like I said, he's a big country fan."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Mark Brachecki as Video Drummer
xref.body: The drummer seen in the music video for "She Sells Sanctuary" was Mark Brachecki, who was on loan from the band Big Country, as Nigel Preston had already been fired. "The drummer we see in the video for Sanctuary is a dude named Mark Brachecki, who was on loan from the band Big Country."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Musical Vision
xref.body: Kid Rock had a distinct musical vision, which he described as "very white trash Public Enemy style rap, plus The Stooges, plus Kiss, plus Hank Williams," reflecting his broad influences and status as a "big country fan." "He had this vision. A vision he calls very white trash public enemy style rap, plus the stooge's plus kiss plus Hank Williams. Like I said, he's a big country fan."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Post-Breakup Projects
xref.body: The group disbanded in 1982, leading its members in different directions. Guitarist Stuart Adamson went on to form Big Country, one of the most successful Scottish bands of the 1980s. "The group lasted until 1982 when they cleaved in several different directions. Guitarist Stuart Adamson's next project was Big Country, one of the most successful Scottish bands of the 80s."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
